system_description.narrative_title: Global diesel shortage and geopolitical reshaping of oil supply
system_description.narrative_summary: A pronounced global diesel shortage and record diesel prices—driven by shipping/tanker constraints, regional supply disruptions and drained storage—are rippling through markets and politics. The strain is prompting emergency domestic measures (subsidies, rationing), proposals for export bans, and accelerated diplomatic/ commercial moves to unlock alternative supplies (notably renewed engagement with Venezuela and shifts in trading patterns).
system_description.scope: International diesel and middle-distillate markets including production, refining, storage inventories, tanker and shipping capacity, trading flows and freight rates, related policy responses (export bans, subsidies, rationing), and proximate supply-side diplomacy and commercial deals (Venezuelan re-engagement, maker-operator actions by oil firms).
system_description.super_system: Global energy system (fossil-fuel commodity markets, refining/transport infrastructures, and geopolitics)
adjacent_subsystems: International finance, sanctions and commodity trading
Domestic political economy and energy policy (e.g., export bans, subsidies)
Alternative fuels and refining capacity (biodiesel, jet fuel balancing)

variables.name: Middle-distillate production flow
variables.description: The volumetric rate at which refineries produce diesel and other middle-distillate fuels for the market.

variables.name: Refinery conversion capacity
variables.description: The aggregated maximum capability of refining infrastructure to convert crude oil into middle-distillate products.

variables.name: Refinery utilization rate
variables.description: The proportion of available refining capacity that is actively operating at a given time.

variables.name: Diesel storage inventory
variables.description: The total volume of diesel and equivalent middle-distillate held in commercial and strategic storage across the system.

variables.name: Tanker availability and capacity
variables.description: The effective shipping tonnage and number of tankers available for transporting middle distillates across shipping routes.

variables.name: Freight rate level
variables.description: The prevailing cost per unit-distance to move middle-distillate cargoes by sea, reflecting shipping market tightness.

variables.name: Cross-border trade flow volumes
variables.description: The volume of diesel and related distillates shipped between regions and countries per unit time.

variables.name: Domestic consumption rate
variables.description: The rate at which end-users within consuming regions are burning or using diesel for transport, industry, and agriculture.

variables.name: Alternative fuel substitution rate
variables.description: The rate at which diesel demand is replaced by alternatives (e.g., biodiesel blends, LNG, electrification) over time.

variables.name: Diesel price level
variables.description: The market price per unit of diesel, reflecting current supply-demand balance and market signals.

variables.name: Price volatility
variables.description: The short- to medium-term variability and amplitude of fluctuations in diesel and middle-distillate prices.

variables.name: Export restrictions intensity
variables.description: The degree to which policy frameworks constrain or limit cross-border exports of diesel and middle distillates.

variables.name: Fuel subsidy and rationing intensity
variables.description: The scale and prevalence of domestic interventions such as subsidies, price controls, and rationing applied to diesel consumers.

variables.name: Shipping network congestion
variables.description: The level of logistical bottlenecks and capacity constraints in maritime and port networks relevant to distillate movements.

variables.name: Storage drawdown rate
variables.description: The pace at which diesel inventories are being depleted from storage reservoirs over a given period.

variables.name: Geopolitical tension level
variables.description: The intensity of international political and security frictions that affect energy supply routes, trade relationships, and market risk perceptions.

catalysts.title: US diesel export ban decision
catalysts.description: A White House decision whether to ban US diesel exports following political pressure ahead of the 2026 midterms.

catalysts.title: Venezuela re-engagement and output restart
catalysts.description: Deals with TotalEnergies and ongoing Venezuelan debt/energy talks could unlock Venezuelan crude/diesel exports and production.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'TotalEnergies signs deal paving way for return to Venezuela' and 'Venezuelan delegation... seeking debt, energy deals.'

catalysts.title: Tanker shortage and shipping-rate spike
catalysts.description: Ongoing shortage of oil tankers keeps freight rates elevated and constrains cross-border middle-distillate movements.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Tanker Shortage Sends Oil-Shipping Rates Soaring' and 'A Shortage of Oil Tankers Is Threatening to Keep Gas Prices High.'

catalysts.title: Storage drawdown continuing into 2027
catalysts.description: Inventories and strategic tanks are being drawn down, maintaining shortage conditions into 2027.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Global diesel shortage likely to last into 2027 as storage tanks drain.'

catalysts.title: Petrobras joins diesel subsidy program
catalysts.description: Brazil's Petrobras approved joining a diesel subsidy program, likely expanding domestic subsidies and demand.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Brazil's Petrobras board approves joining diesel subsidy program.'

catalysts.title: European Q4 jet-fuel supply deficit
catalysts.description: Expected Q4 jet-fuel shortfall increases competition for middle distillates, drawing product away from diesel markets.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Europe faces Q4 jet fuel supply deficit even as South Korea becomes latest big supplier.'

catalysts.title: Russia reroutes diesel to Central Asia
catalysts.description: Elevated Russian diesel exports to Central Asia alter regional flows and availability elsewhere.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Russia boosted diesel exports to Central Asia in August, traders say.'

catalysts.title: Biodiesel becomes cheaper for shipping
catalysts.description: Falling biodiesel prices for shipping make substitution more economical, reducing conventional diesel bunkering demand.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Biodiesel for shipping now cheaper than conventional fuels after price fall.'
